anita_malhotra: FYI ran the nightly microburst suite, host ingress 95th jumped ~42% for the tiny-req streaming profile. noticing CPU pinned in host-side parse/tokenize path. attaching quick pprof snapshot below.

anita_malhotra: pprof snippet:
```
40.1%  tokenize::state::reset
25.7%  parse::read_frame
12.3%  grpc::streaming::write_small_chunks
8.4%   kernel_selector::choose (batch=1)
```

sam_lee: small-chunk workload = lots of single-line prompts + streaming tokens, right?

kevin_w: yep. two observations:
1) kernel selector is choosing quant-unpack_v2 for batch=1 which has higher host preproc overhead (we measured this earlier).
2) we do many tiny syscalls because the stream chunking layer emits sub-128B writes frequently. writev coalesce is enabled but windowing is too tight.

taylor_ops: can you paste the selector log lines?

kevin_w: paste:
```
[2026-03-18T02:11:12Z] req_id=aa4 kernel_choice=quant_unpack_v2 seq=24 batch=1 reason=low_latency_hint
[2026-03-18T02:11:12Z] req_id=bb7 kernel_choice=fused_fp16 seq=128 batch=8 reason=throughput_hint
```

sam_lee: ok that matches. for tiny-reqs, the host tokenizer reset alloc shows up in samples because we create/tear tokenizer state per request. reusing the tokenizer scratch would avoid a lot of alloc+memset.

anita_malhotra: other quick wins?

taylor_ops: bumping the coalesce window from 4ms -> 12ms lowered syscall count in previous tests. tradeoff: slightly higher first-byte latency on tiny streams (~5–10ms) but 95th improves. we should gate by customer tier.

kevin_w: also KV cache: noticed high miss churn because prefix-normalization wasn't applied for streaming partial keys. small partial keys evict hot entries. normalization hook fixes that.

anita_malhotra: proposed immediate triage steps: 1) reuse tokenizer buffer pool, 2) increase writev coalesce-window for streaming route, 3) add streaming-key normalization, 4) add kernel-selector soft-fallback: if batch==1 and seq<64 prefer fused_fp16 microkernel if available.

sam_lee: I can do #1 and #2 in a single host-side patch (token-buffer pool + coalesce param). low-risk.

kevin_w: I'll prototype selector tweak + add a metric to count quant_unpacked_batch1 hits.

taylor_ops: I'll add a canary config for coalesce-window per-customer-tier and wire it into console rollouts.

deploy-bot: New PR opened: <https://git.internal/redwood/host/commit/ae9f3d> (#3412) by sam_lee — "host: tokenizer pool + streaming coalesce window"

infra-bot: Canary started: canary-143 on prod-edge-us-east-1 (10% traffic)

anita_malhotra: quick canary numbers after 30m:
- 95th host ingress latency: down 18%
- host CPU samples in tokenize::reset: down 62%
- syscall write count: down 54%

sam_lee: flakiness check looks fine. no obvious error spikes in logs.

kevin_w: my selector patch is ready as a follow-up PR (#3419). tests show for batch=1+seq<=48 fused_fp16 path reduces host preproc by ~12% and decode latency by ~6% in microbench. will gate behind a feature flag.

anita_malhotra: great. next actions: ship #3412 to prod (full rollout) after 4h canary, merge #3419 behind flag and run perf-canary for 24h against tiny-req suite, and add a KV-normalization hotfix (#3424) to reduce cache churn.

taylor_ops: scheduling rollout: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 hours if metrics stay green. I'll add rollback playbook.

sam_lee: patch pushed to prod canary -> promoting after 4h. link: <https://console.redwood/canaries/143>

anita_malhotra: thanks all. follow-up: create a short note in eng-runtime channel with before/after pprof and the selector histogram. capture a synthetic run for tiny-req streaming and tag customer-impacting tickets.

kevin_w: filed perf ticket: <https://issues.redwood/RT-1987> — includes flamegraphs and selector histograms.

anita_malhotra: OK closing thread. If anyone sees a regression post-rollout ping here. :thumbsup:
